title: EXP-095 - Hello World Part 6 Section 3: FX_Orders Event Handler FX_CalcOrderTotal (Form Script Method CalcOrderTotal), Data Change on FX_ItemCombobox and FX_CountEdit, One Designer Save, Runtime Recalculation Check
objective: Follow hello-world-pt6.md Section 3 (02:05-03:43), adapted to FX_ names and User scope: on the FX_Orders Form in the Web Designer, read the Script Editor's Compile Result panel once (read-only), make one new event handler with the custom event name FX_CalcOrderTotal, Response Type Form Script Method, method CalcOrderTotal and parameters P(FX_Count),P(FX_ItmsCost), then set Data Change = FX_CalcOrderTotal on FX_ItemCombobox and FX_CountEdit, and perform exactly one Designer Save. Verify persistence after one Designer close/reopen. Then in the Web Client, on order 1, change Count 2 -> 3 and Item dumbbell -> eggs without saving, record whether Order Total recalculates before Save, discard with close + No, and verify both orders unchanged after a reopen. Grid columns (Section 4) are a later experiment. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt6.md Section 3 and its transcript lines (02:05-03:43), docs/mongoose/scripts/FX_Orders-form-script.vb (the saved form script, for reference only), recipes/components/apply-component-class.md (the runtime steps and pitfalls), recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-093 and EXP-094 records. Do not read those records in full.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-095-hello-world-part-6-section-3-fx-orders-calc-order-total-event.md and evidence/EXP-095/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task; never sign in inside the portal's embedded app frame (refused, EXP-080-R2) but use the procedure's top-level portal navigation. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, menu or unsaved runtime change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action.

Designer gate (read-only): the Designer is in User scope and clean on FX_Orders (Save and Undo disabled; open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry if needed); Behavior > Script Language reads Visual Basic; the Details > Event Handlers grid has no rows; the Data Change field of FX_ItemCombobox and FX_CountEdit is blank. If the Designer is not clean, a handler row already exists, or the session shows the server-event error, record it and stop blocked.

Compile Result (read-only): open the Script Editor once with the blue pencil (Form selected), confirm its content still contains Public Sub CalcOrderTotal, expand the collapsible Compile Result panel by one view click and record its full content verbatim with a screenshot (record an empty panel as empty). Never click into or type in the editor text. Leave it with Cancel once. If Save is enabled afterwards, record it and stop blocked for the operator.

Event handler: open Details > Event Handlers and use New once. Record every field of the new-handler form or dialog with its exact labels before filling it. Set the event name to FX_CalcOrderTotal (choose it from a list if offered, otherwise type it once), Response Type to Form Script Method, and in the Parameters (...) dialog choose the method CalcOrderTotal from its list and enter the parameter string P(FX_Count),P(FX_ItmsCost) in that order (OrderCount first, ItemCost second). Leave every other field at its default and record it. Confirm the dialogs with OK and read back the handler row (event name, sequence, response type, disabled flag, method and parameter summary) with a screenshot. If a value reads back wrong, make at most one correction per field, then read back again; if it is still wrong, record both values and stop blocked without Save.

Component events: select FX_ItemCombobox in the Details > Components grid (or the Properties component selector), set its Events > Data Change field to FX_CalcOrderTotal (choose from its drop-down; type the exact name only if it is not listed) and commit it; read it back with a screenshot. Do the same once for FX_CountEdit. Never set Primary, Lose Focus, Gain Focus or any other field, and never change any other component, including the grid columns. At most one correction per field.

Perform exactly one Designer Save through the native toolbar Save and record its native response verbatim (toast, dialog or error) with a screenshot. If an error appears, record it and stop blocked; never retry the Save.

Persistence: close the clean FX_Orders Designer Form once through its Form-tab control (record any prompt; if a save prompt appears, answer No once and record its text) and reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry. Verify Save is disabled; read back the Event Handlers row and the Data Change value of FX_ItemCombobox and FX_CountEdit (open no handler dialog for the readback unless the grid does not show the method and parameters; then open it once and leave it with Cancel). If Save is enabled after the readback, close once answering No and reopen once to restore clean; if it is still enabled, record it and stop blocked.

Runtime baseline (read-only): in the Web Client, if FX_Orders is open close it once (clean); open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (operator-approved route, EXP-093), switch to Filter in Place if needed, leave every criterion blank and press F4 once; verify order 1: Customer ID FX001, Customer Name Factory test one, Address 1 Factory Street, Item dumbbell, Item Description 45 pound iron, Cost 45.00, Count 2, Order Total 90.00 and order 2: Customer ID FX002, Customer Name Factory test two, Address 2 Factory Street, Item eggs, Item Description cage free, Cost 6.99, Count 1, Order Total 6.99 (move between orders only by clicking their row-number cells).

Runtime Count check: on order 1 click the detail-view Count field once, select its whole content, type 3 once, press Tab once, and record without any Save the Count, Cost and Order Total in the detail view and the order 1 grid row, with a screenshot. Expected by the tutorial: Order Total 135.00 before Save; record whatever is shown, and any message or error verbatim (acknowledge an error once and continue to the discard).

Runtime Item check: still on order 1 and still unsaved, open the FX_ItemCombobox drop-down once and choose eggs once; record Item, Item Description, Cost, Count and Order Total in the detail view and the grid row, with a screenshot. Expected if the cost updates before the event: Cost 6.99 and Order Total 20.97 (3 x 6.99); if the event runs first, Order Total may stay 135.00. Record whatever is shown as observed only.

Discard: close the runtime FX_Orders Form once; answer No once to the prompt to save changes and record its exact text; if any other prompt appears answer No once and record its exact text; if no save prompt appears, record it and stop blocked for the coordinator without further action. Then reopen FX_Orders once through the recent-forms entry (blank criteria, F4 once; row-number cells only) and verify order 1: Customer ID FX001, Customer Name Factory test one, Address 1 Factory Street, Item dumbbell, Item Description 45 pound iron, Cost 45.00, Count 2, Order Total 90.00 and order 2: Customer ID FX002, Customer Name Factory test two, Address 2 Factory Street, Item eggs, Item Description cage free, Cost 6.99, Count 1, Order Total 6.99 unchanged. Close the runtime FX_Orders Form once at the end (clean).

Capture screenshots of the Designer gate, the Compile Result panel, the new-handler form before and after filling, the Parameters dialog before OK, the handler row, each Data Change readback, the Save response, the reopened Designer readbacks, the runtime baseline, order 1 after the Count change, order 1 after the Item change, the save prompt before answering, and the reopened orders.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.

notes: Proposed by the operator assistant after EXP-094 (handoff-after-exp-094); the operator said yes on 2026-10-15 and chose the custom event name FX_CalcOrderTotal. Tenant mapping: tutorial Calc Order Total -> event FX_CalcOrderTotal; form-script method CalcOrderTotal(OrderCount, ItemCost) saved in EXP-094 (writes FX_DerOrderTotal, derived FX_Count * FX_ItmsCost, Read Only since EXP-081); tutorial P(Count),P(ItmsCost) -> P(FX_Count),P(FX_ItmsCost). EXP-094 did not establish compile success, so the read-only Compile Result check comes first and the runtime check is the real test. In EXP-093 the unsaved Count 3 left Order Total 90.00; with the handler the tutorial expects 135.00 before Save. The Item change also tests the event order: 20.97 means FX_ItmsCost updated before the event. Both runtime changes are discarded with close + No and the reopen verifies both orders. Grid columns (Section 4) are a later experiment. The EXP-094 prohibited pattern against creating event handlers is replaced by one against removing them, because creating one handler is the authorized action. exact_values: FX_Orders, FX_CalcOrderTotal, CalcOrderTotal, Form Script Method, P(FX_Count),P(FX_ItmsCost), FX_ItemCombobox, FX_CountEdit, 135.00, 20.97, FX001, FX002, dumbbell, eggs. deny_browser_javascript.
